newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 29.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime minister John Howard will take 10-point Wik plan to Parliament following a special Premiers Conference yesterday where his 10-point response to the High Court's controversial Wik ruling received broad endorsement from all State and Territory leaders - except Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge - Howard announced he would put his plan into law, defying demands to extinguish native title on pastoral leases. Page 1.

In his first major speech since his appointment as a deputy-governor of the Reserve Bank late last year, Stephen Grenville warned yesterday union efforts to seek flow-on wage rises through the award system could threaten Australia's low inflation rate. Page 3.

Following a nine-month investigation by the Australian Federal Police into allegations that National MP Michael Cobb rorted parliamentary entitlements, Cobb faces six charges of fraud and five of making an untrue representation following a mention in the CT Magistrates Court yesterday. Page 3.

Under the Logan Review of the Attorney-General's Legal Practice, released yesterday by Federal Attorney-General Daryl Williams who revealed it had been approved by Cabinet, private law firms will soon be able to compete for Federal Government litigation work, worth at least A$30 million. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard plans to rush legislation into Parliament next month to protect graziers and miners from native title claims after holding successful talks with State and Territory leaders in Canberra yesterday, where he won the backing of all premiers, except Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge, for his 10-point native title plan. Page 1.

Yesterday, around 1pm on the one-year anniversary of the Port Arthur massacre, Walter Mikac, who has become the prime symbol of personal loss in the tragedy after his wife and two young daughters were fatally shot by Martin Bryant, left a personal memorial to his family near a gum tree where they were killed. Page 1.

Steel unions are planning a national campaign supported by the ACTU against all BHP industries after it was revealed the Big Australian is to close the country's biggest steelworks at Newcastle, causing the loss of 2,000 jobs on site and a further 5,000 in supporting industries, slashing A$2 billion a year from the Hunter economy in New South Wales. Page 1.

The ABC will be forced to cut at least A$10 million from its domestic programs after Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer revealed yesterday the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade will provide A$4 million to allow Radio Australia to keep some short-waveservices, sparing the national broadcaster the main burden of funding the scaled-down RA service that Cabinet agreed to last week. Page 3.

THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD Despite failing to win the endorsement of Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge and Western Australian Premier Richard Court, who both expressed serious concerns with Prime Minister John Howard's 10-point response to the High Court's Wik decision, Howard went public on his proposals for the first time yesterday - vowing effectively to extinguish native title on pastoral leases. Page 1.

According to the surprise findings of a four-year Telstra-funded study by Royal Adelaide Hospital, mice exposed to electro-magnetic radiation equivalent to spending one hour a day on a digital mobile phone are twice as likely to develop lymphoma, a cancer of the immune system. Page 1.

As Australians all around the country held services and paused for a minute's silence, 500 people attended the Moving On memorial service yesterday in the ruins of Port Arthur's convict-built church to mourn the deaths of the 35 people killed a year befor at the hands of lone gunman Martin Bryant. Page 1.

Following the release of a new Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics study which found that a proposed global reduction in greenhouse gas emissions to 10 per cent below 1990 levels by 2020 would cost every Australian A$9,000, Prime Minister John Howard will warn Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto today that adoption of mandatory reduction targets would be economically detrimental to both countries. Page 3.
THE AGE

Despite the fact that Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge, Aboriginal negotiators and farmers' groups have not yet endorsed his 10-point response to the High Court's controversial Wik ruling, Prime Minister John Howard plans to proceed with his plan after yesterday getting the support of the majority of States. Page 1.

Five hundred people, including Governor-General Sir William Deane, attended the Moving On memorial service in the remains of Port Arthur's convict-built church yesterday to mark the one-year anniversary of Martin Bryant's massacre, which resulted in the daths of 35 people. Page 1.

It has been revealed Raywood Communications, a leading communications company, contacted Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett three times and the then State Health Minister Marie Tehan in 1993 to express concerns about the tendering process for Victoria's ambulance dispatch system. Page 1.

In an open rebuff to Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, who has blocked Australia's attempts to win a seat at summit meetings of Asian and European leaders, Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said last night Australia should be allowed to articipate in the Asia-Europe talks as an Asian member. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
